correctness.rationale: Paley difference counts are derived from elementary Legendre-character correlation. Orthogonality gives the normalized fourth moment as the sum of squared autocorrelations; sharp Cauchy and the power-mean inequality establish the claimed constant. All equality requires constant moduli and a difference phase function. That function is additive for p≥31 by the squarefree-cubic Weil bound with explicit root correction; for p=19,23 by exact exhaustive pair enumeration. For p=11 the four necessary phase equations have exponent determinant magnitude eleven, yielding exactly the eleven character phases. For p=7 each difference is unique, so all equal-modulus phases qualify. The package-local checker ran and passed 335 indexed exact checks; finite checks supplement rather than replace infinite proofs. The only external analytic lemma is the standard Weil cubic sum bound.

originality.rationale: Primary and semantically closest published findings were compared at the level of objects, moment normalization, coefficient quantifiers and equality implications, not titles alone. Classical Paley difference multiplicity gives the norm constant but does not by itself supply the full extremizer variety or the p=7/p=11 transition. The closest accessible Paley L4 article optimizes asymptotic aperiodic Littlewood merit factors rather than this periodic unrestricted maximum. Finite-field extension papers address paraboloid/cone supports, and other published phase papers treat different finite spectra. A possible old difference-set equality theorem or general Freiman-extension formulation remains a disclosed residual bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: The additive quadratic-residue difference set is a canonical and widely studied spectrum. The theorem gives the sharp Fourier L2-to-L4 norm with unrestricted coefficients and completely classifies the equality geometry. The abrupt change from a full two-torus of projective phases at p=7 to exactly p character phases at all larger admissible primes is a motivated structural rigidity phenomenon, not a merely numerical special case, and requires nontrivial cubic-character and phase-relation arguments. It supplies a reusable exact extremizer model for finite harmonic analysis.
